app.name: ServiceNow
app.category: ITSM / enterprise platform (instance REST API and OAuth 2.0 provider)

verdict.summary: There is no central ServiceNow app registry and no managed OAuth app in Composio, so you register an OAuth application record inside each customer instance you connect to. That per-instance setup is quick, but listing for all customers goes through Build Partner enrollment and Store certification, which takes weeks.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for one instance (admin access required); 1-2 weeks of your work plus 3-5 weeks of certification for a Store listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min if you have admin rights on an instance
verdict.approval_wait: None for per-instance registration. Store certification: 3-5 weeks (reported by ServiceNow). Build Partner enrollment time not found.

gates.name: Own-instance OAuth application (no review)
gates.unlocks: Create an OAuth application record in an instance you administer and connect your own account through Composio using that client ID and secret.
limits: Registration is per instance; the record lives in the customer instance's System OAuth > Application Registry (or Machine Identity Console on newer releases).
Store-installed apps cannot be installed on a Personal Developer Instance, so a PDI cannot test a Store-installed build.
No ServiceNow install cap or user limit for unreviewed OAuth apps was found; do not assume one.
Access and refresh token lifespans are set on the registry record and are configurable.

gates.name: Build Partner access (Store Publisher Portal)
gates.unlocks: Access to the Store Publisher Portal and a limited number of vendor instances, which is required before any Store listing.
limits: You must be a Build Partner to list an app on the ServiceNow Store; non-participants must join the Partner Program first.
A 2026 Access tier lets partners start building before full enrollment.
The Jan 2026 release moves global partners to a single annual fee; the amount is not stated. An older guide lists $5,000 USD, which may be outdated.
Tiered benefits are tied to Store outcomes.
gates.time_to_reach: Not found in research; depends on Build Partner enrollment

gates.name: Store listing (ServiceNow Store certification)
gates.unlocks: A Store listing that customers can install without custom registration work, subject to certification.
limits: Two tracks: App review (design doc, test plan, installation guide) and Listing review (marketing docs, demo videos, branding).
Store upgrades with no code change: reported 1-2 days; full reviews reported up to about 7 days.
Certified apps can require recertification for new releases and after code changes.
Apps with no code or business logic are not recommended; global-scope prototypes are reported as not certifiable.
gates.time_to_reach: 3-5 weeks from submission to publish-ready (ServiceNow's typical estimate), plus any fix turnaround

steps.title: Confirm instance access and release
steps.detail: Confirm you have an admin role on a ServiceNow instance you can use for testing, and check which release it runs. Newer releases manage inbound integrations in the Machine Identity Console, while older ones use System OAuth > Application Registry. Custom OAuth scopes are reported from around the Tokyo release onward.
gotchas: Do not use a PDI to test a Store-installed app; Store apps cannot be installed on PDIs.

steps.title: Create the OAuth application record
steps.detail: In System OAuth > Application Registry, click New and choose the option to create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients. Enter a Name and the Redirect URL, then save. Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the Redirect URL field.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The Redirect URL field is reported as mandatory for configuration since March 24, 2021 (community source).

steps.title: Choose the grant type
steps.detail: For a user-connected flow brokered by Composio, use the authorization-code grant. The redirect URL is a callback resource in the connecting application, so it must match Composio's callback. The client-credentials grant does not use the redirect or login URL and is not the right choice for per-user connections.

steps.title: Keep the client confidential
steps.detail: Leave the Public Client option off. Only confidential clients should use the client-credentials flow, and the same record is used for the secret exchange. Save the record once the redirect URL is set.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the saved registry record. In Composio's ServiceNow auth config, enter them along with the per-instance authorize and token URLs for your instance subdomain.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Set token lifespans
steps.detail: In the registry record's advanced options, set the access token lifespan and the refresh token lifespan. Third-party guides show different values (14400 s access; 7,776,000 s or 8,640,000 s refresh), so pick values that match your session policy and check them against your instance's current defaults.
gotchas: The example values come from third-party guides, not ServiceNow's docs; the values differ between sources.

steps.title: Decide scope and access restrictions
steps.detail: The standard scope is useraccount, which covers account information and preferences. If your release supports custom auth scopes, define one only for the REST resources you need. Strict mode is on by default for new clients; keep it on unless you need broader access, since disabling it lets the client reach APIs not tied to any auth scope. Check Enforce Token Restriction and OAuth entity linking, because a policy linked to another OAuth app will deny yours.

values.label: Strict mode
values.value: Allow access only to APIs in selected scope (default on)

values.label: Enforce Token Restriction
values.value: Off by default; requires the API Access Policy linked to the OAuth entity

gotchas: ServiceNow access control is the most common source of Store review findings (community source).

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: From Composio, connect your own account to the ServiceNow instance. If you use client credentials instead, confirm the system property glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled is set in Global scope and that an OAuth application user with a suitable role exists. A Zurich-release user reported server_error and access_denied after a client-credentials setup; no fix is shown in that thread.
gotchas: If you see server_error or access_denied, first re-check the redirect URL, client ID and secret, and any linked API access policy.

steps.title: Confirm Build Partner status
steps.detail: If you want a Store listing, join the ServiceNow Partner Program and enroll as a Build Partner. Check the current 2026 fee and tier criteria directly with ServiceNow, since the amount was not stated in the release and the figure found is from an older guide.
gotchas: Do not budget on the $5,000 figure without confirming it; it predates the 2026 redesign.

steps.title: Draft certification materials
steps.detail: An agent can draft the design doc, test plan, installation guide, marketing copy, and a demo-video script for the App review and Listing review tracks. The app needs a working use case with real code or business logic, not an integration-only shell, and it must be scoped rather than global-scope.

steps.title: Record demo videos and assets
steps.detail: Record the demo videos and prepare branding for the Listing review track. These are human actions and cannot be done by an agent.

steps.title: Submit through the Store Publisher Portal
steps.detail: Submit the app in the Store Publisher Portal and track progress from the Certify tab, which shows App Review and Listing Review separately. Send certification questions to certifiers@servicenow.com.

steps.title: Wait for certification
steps.detail: ServiceNow typically takes 3-5 weeks from submission to publish-ready, depending on app size, documentation, and turnaround on fixes. Upgrade reviews with no code change may be quicker. Plan for recertification after future releases or code changes.

requirements.detail: Needed to create the registry record and set token lifespans.

scopes.effect: Default and, per community reports, the only scope on the standard provider. Covers account information and preferences. No sensitivity tier was found.
Reported on newer releases (from around Tokyo). Can be tied to specific REST resources. Strict mode then restricts the client to APIs in its scope.
Lets the client reach APIs not tied to any auth scope. Expands what reviewers look at; avoid unless required.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with server_error and access_denied after a client-credentials setup (Zurich release reported).
blockers.cause: Not resolved in the source thread; likely a configuration mismatch (client credentials, role, property, or linked access policy).
blockers.fix: Check the client ID and secret, the OAuth application user role, the glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled property in Global scope, and any API access policy linked to another OAuth entity. No vendor fix is documented in the findings.
blockers.contact: ServiceNow community forum or your ServiceNow support channel

blockers.symptom: Cannot test a Store-installed app on a Personal Developer Instance.
blockers.cause: Store apps cannot be installed on PDIs.
blockers.fix: Test on a non-PDI instance you control, or use the customer's sandbox instance.

blockers.symptom: Cannot list the app on the ServiceNow Store.
blockers.fix: Join the ServiceNow Partner Program and enroll as a Build Partner before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Store certification flags the app as a global-scope prototype or as lacking business logic.
blockers.cause: Certification discourages integration-only apps with no code, and global-scope prototypes are reported as not certifiable.
blockers.fix: Build a scoped app with a working use case and standard files before submission.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow. Start on your own app: register an OAuth application record in each customer instance and paste its client ID and secret into Composio. Per-instance URLs are https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do. Composio's default redirect URI must be entered as the Redirect URL in the registry record.

evidence.claim: Composio toolkit lookup: no managed OAuth for ServiceNow; OAUTH2 mode uses per-instance authorize/token URLs with default scope useraccount.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": false

evidence.claim: Custom OAuth scopes are available on newer ServiceNow releases (a community answer dates the change to the Tokyo release).
evidence.quote: It seems from Tokyo onwards; you can configure your own auth scopes.

evidence.claim: A ServiceNow developer article says the 'useraccount' scope stays available alongside API Authentication Scopes, which can be tied to specific REST resources, such as one close resource on the Interaction Management API.
evidence.quote: the default `useraccount` scope remains available

evidence.claim: New OAuth clients default to a strict mode ('Allow access only to APIs in selected scope'); disabling it makes the client broadly scoped, which also allows APIs not tied to any auth scope.
evidence.quote: When enabled (default for new OAuth clients): The OAuth client can only access APIs that are explicitly associated with its assigned Auth Scope.

evidence.claim: Enforce Token Restriction is a separate OAuth entity setting that is disabled by default and requires the API Access Policy to be explicitly linked to the OAuth entity.
evidence.quote: Within the OAuth entity configuration, there's a setting called

evidence.claim: OAuth Entity Linking limits an API access policy to one named OAuth application, so other OAuth apps are denied even when they meet the policy conditions.
evidence.quote: Only the linked OAuth app can access the API through that policy.

evidence.claim: Client-credentials registrations need an OAuth application user with an appropriate role, and the grant must be enabled through a global-scope system property (glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled).
evidence.quote: Yes the property "glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled" must be in Global scope.

evidence.claim: The client-credentials setup guide says it requires an admin role and asks that the Public Client option not be set, because only confidential clients should use that flow.
evidence.quote: only confidential clients should use this flow.

evidence.claim: Access token lifespan is configurable in the registry's advanced options; one third-party integration guide sets it to 14400 seconds.
evidence.quote: change the Access token lifespan to 14400 seconds.

evidence.claim: Refresh token lifespan is set on the OAuth application record; a Microsoft integration guide lists 7,776,000 seconds (90 days) for this field.
evidence.quote: change the Refresh Token Lifespan to 7,776,000 seconds (90 days).

evidence.claim: A community poster set the refresh token lifespan on a sample registration to 8,640,000 seconds.
evidence.quote: Refresh Token Lifespan: 8640000 seconds

evidence.claim: OAuth app registration happens inside a ServiceNow instance: the admin creates an application record by choosing the option to create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients in System OAuth > Application Registry.
evidence.quote: Give the provider a Name and Redirect URL.

evidence.claim: Composio's default redirect URI for ServiceNow is its own backend callback, which would need to be registered as the Redirect URL when Composio brokers the flow.

open_questions: No ServiceNow announcement found that sets an install cap, user limit, or distribution cap for unlisted OAuth apps. Absence is not proof; confirm with ServiceNow Partner or Store contacts.
No list of ServiceNow scopes classed as sensitive or restricted was found, so scope tiers are marked unknown.
Current 2026 Build Partner fee and tier criteria were not found; the $5,000 figure is from an older guide.

The Store Publisher Portal KB (KB0030070) and the official OAuth configuration docs were not fetched; details rely on search snippets and community posts. The Store KB (KB1270874) returned no body text.
Whether one OAuth app can serve many customer instances, or each customer admin must create a registry record, was not confirmed. Sources describe per-instance registration.
Redirect URL matching rules (exact match, wildcards, http vs https, localhost) were not confirmed from an official source.
PKCE support for the authorization-code flow was not confirmed.
No official review timeline, privacy-policy, domain-verification, or minimum-install requirement was found for a customer-installed app outside the Store.
